content.text:
Create a new branch and fix this issue. Once done push your changes.

Property assignment frees its operands mid-insert (src/vm.zig:509). OP_SET_PROPERTY pops the value and the receiver, then calls fields.put. If the hash map grows, that allocation can trigger a collection while neither value is on the stack. Confirmed: f.name = "hel" + "lo"; print f.name; printed garbage bytes, and Foo().x = 1; freed the instance while its field map was being grown, which trips the map's safety lock in Debug and corrupts the heap in release. Fix: peek instead of pop, and only pop after the put.

Keep property assignment operands rooted during insert

OP_SET_PROPERTY popped the value and receiver before calling fields.put.
Growing the field map allocates, which can trigger a collection while
neither operand is on the stack: a freshly built string value was freed
(printing garbage), and a temporary receiver like `Foo().x = 1` was freed
while its own map was being grown. Peek at both operands instead and only
pop them after the put.

Add a Heap.stressGc flag that collects before every allocation. A single
low threshold can't hit this bug: temporary peaks earlier in the program
trigger the one collection and reset the threshold to 1 MiB.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
I fixed the bug on a new branch, `fix-set-property-gc`, and pushed it. All 86 tests pass, with and without `-Dnan-boxing=true`, and `zig fmt --check` is clean. I didn't open a PR.

**The fix** (`src/vm.zig`): `OP_SET_PROPERTY` now peeks at the value and the receiver instead of popping them. Both pop only after `fields.put` returns, so they stay on the stack, and safe from the GC, while the field map grows.

**The test needed a change to the GC.** Setting `threshold = 1`, as the existing stress test does, never reproduces this bug. Hash-map resizes briefly keep the old and new buffers alive together, and that peak always crosses the threshold before the `put` does. The one collection runs there, and the threshold then jumps to at least 1 MiB. So I added a small `stressGc` flag to `Heap` (`src/heap.zig`). When it's on, the threshold stays at 0, so a collection runs before every allocation, like the book's `DEBUG_STRESS_GC`.

**Regression test:** a new fixture, `samples/060_set_property_gc.lox`, and test `060 set property survives garbage collection` in `engine.zig` cover both cases from the report. Before the fix it hit the same pointer-stability panic you saw in Debug; after the fix it passes.

One trap if you write a similar test: comparing `f.name` against the literal `"hello"` hides the bug. Strings are interned, so `"hel" + "lo"` resolves to the literal's constant, which is always reachable and never freed. The fixture compares against a second concatenation instead.
